questions.question: What problem do virtual environments solve?
options: They speed up Python script execution
They allow each project to have its own isolated package versions, preventing conflicts
They enable Python code to run on different operating systems
They automatically update packages to the latest version
questions.explanation: Without virtual environments, all projects share one global Python installation. If Project A needs Django 3.2 and Project B needs Django 4.2, they conflict. Virtual environments give each project its own isolated site-packages directory.

questions.question: What command creates a new virtual environment named `venv`?
options: `pip create venv`
`virtualenv create venv`
`python -m venv venv`
`python --virtualenv venv`
questions.explanation: `python -m venv venv` runs the built-in `venv` module (available since Python 3.3) to create a new virtual environment in the `venv` directory. The second `venv` is just the folder name—you can use any name.

questions.question: Should you commit the `venv/` folder to git?
options: Yes, so teammates can use the same environment without reinstalling
No—it is large, platform-specific, and reproducible from `requirements.txt`
Only if the project uses Python 3.10 or newer
Yes, but only the `lib/` subdirectory
questions.explanation: The `venv/` directory can be hundreds of megabytes, contains platform-specific binaries that won't work on other operating systems, and can be recreated from `requirements.txt`. Always add it to `.gitignore`.

questions.question: How can you verify that a virtual environment is currently active?
options: Run `python --check-venv`
The terminal prompt shows `(venv)` prefix, and `which python` points inside the venv directory
The `pip list` command shows zero packages
Python runs twice as fast
questions.explanation: When a venv is activated, the shell prepends its name to your prompt (e.g., `(venv)`). You can also run `which python` (macOS/Linux) or `where python` (Windows)—it should show a path inside the venv folder.

questions.question: What is the correct workflow for a new team member setting up a project?
options: Copy the `venv/` folder from the team lead
Run `pip install` for each package individually from memory
Create a new venv, activate it, then run `pip install -r requirements.txt`
Install packages globally with `sudo pip install`
questions.explanation: The standard onboarding workflow: (1) clone the repo, (2) create a fresh venv with `python -m venv venv`, (3) activate it, (4) install dependencies with `pip install -r requirements.txt`. This ensures an identical, isolated environment.
